note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old man with 3 days of watery diarrhoea preceded by brief vomiting; probable gastroenteritis per clinician.
- Advised oral rehydration (Dioralyte), paracetamol PRN, remain off work until symptom-free; review if not improved in one week.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute watery diarrhoea, onset 3 days ago; frequency ~5–6 bowel movements/day.
- Initial vomiting for a couple of episodes that has since resolved.
- Associated symptoms: subjective feeling of fever/was warm early on, current generalized weakness, reduced appetite, poor oral intake.
- No visible blood in stool; no significant abdominal pain reported.
- Systems review: no headache or myalgia reported.
- Social/functional: living alone; off work for past 3 days due to illness.
- Clinician impression: probable gastroenteritis ("tummy bug").
- No physical examination findings or diagnostic tests documented.

Issue 2:
- Risk of dehydration related to frequent watery stools and limited oral intake.
- Patient reports feeling dehydrated and unable to maintain adequate fluid intake because of ongoing diarrhoea.
- No vitals or objective assessment of hydration documented.
- Management discussed: oral fluids and oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) recommended to replenish fluids/electrolytes.

Issue 3:
- Chronic asthma: patient reports having asthma and using a blue inhaler infrequently as needed.
- No recent asthma exacerbation or respiratory symptoms documented in this consult.
- No recent specialist review or pulmonary assessment documented.

Medications:
- Blue inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol — recommended by clinician for fever/weakness; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) — recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No known medication allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.
- Family history: father died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago; mother has type 2 diabetes.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Occupation: software engineer; currently off work for the last 3 days, advised additional 1–2 days until improved.
- Alcohol: drinks infrequently/socially.
- Smoking: denies tobacco use.

Preventative History:
- No information documented regarding cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, FOBT, bone density, vaccinations, recent optometry, or skin checks.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals recorded.
- No clinician-performed physical examination findings documented.
- Patient-reported findings: felt warm early in illness; currently feels weak; vomiting has ceased.

Plan:
- Advise increased oral fluids; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as available.
- Paracetamol for symptomatic relief if febrile or weak (dose not documented).
- Advise remaining off work until diarrhoea-free for 24–48 hours; clinician suggested continuing time off for next day or two.
- If symptoms persist, clinician requested patient return for review next week.
- No diagnostic tests or prescriptions were issued in this consult.

document_quality (quality checks):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP, respiratory rate), physical abdominal examination findings, objective assessment of hydration, stool testing or culture orders, specific medication doses/routes/frequencies.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
- Transcript quality: audible and intelligible overall though with occasional stuttering and minor interruptions; clinical details sufficiently clear.
